problem: The sentence breaks off: "The real path gives ∫δQ/T 3.8)." The comparison and the opening bracket of the cross-reference are missing, so no student can read what the real path gives. The section also never states the important result that the integral along an irreversible path is less than ΔS.
fix: "The real path gives only ∫δQ/T, which is less than ΔS (see 3.8)."

problem: The inequality is missing: "Since cv  T/cp, so the constant-volume line is steeper". As printed there is no relation between cv and cp, and the conclusion does not follow.
fix: "Since cv < cp, T/cv > T/cp, so the constant-volume line is steeper on the T-s diagram."

problem: Same missing inequality: "Since cv  T/cp, so the constant-volume line is steeper." The reasoning step needed to earn the marks is absent.
fix: "The slopes are dT/ds = T/cv at constant volume and dT/ds = T/cp at constant pressure. Since cv < cp, T/cv > T/cp, so the constant-volume line is steeper."

problem: The plotted curves come from air values (cp = 1.005, cv = 0.718 kJ/kg·K, R = 0.287 kJ/kg·K), but the caption and aria text do not say the gas is air, so a student may think the curves hold for any ideal gas. The horizontal axis is labelled s − s₀ while the text uses s.
fix: Caption: "For air (cp = 1.005, cv = 0.718 kJ/kg·K): both curves start at 300 K and rise with entropy; the constant-volume line climbs more steeply than the constant-pressure line." Label the axis "s − s₀ at 300 K, kJ/kg·K" and say the zero of entropy is taken at 300 K.
